pr_title: ddl: prevent 'TEXT' columns without key length from being used in index
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #23488

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

Proposal: [Text column can be used in index without key length #23488](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/23488)

What's Changed:
- Add 1 function checkIndexInModifiableColumn in index.go, refer to checkIndexColumn.
- Add 1 function checkIndexInModifiableColumns in ddl_api.go.
- Add function call to checkIndexInModifiableColumns in checkColumnWithIndexConstraint in ddl_api.go.

How it Works:
As checkIndexColumn already done the check functions during createTable, so we can reuse the logic during alterTable.

### Check List

Tests

- Unit test
- As the function checkColumnWithIndexConstraint is also called by ModifyColumn, but as I donot know much about SQL. I only add TestChangeColumn for the unit test, but donot add TestModifyColumn, so if anyone can give the test scanrio, it would be good.

### Release note
- No release note.

issue_context.title: Text column can be used in index without key length
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
```sql
drop table if exists t;
create table t (k varchar(10) primary key, v int);
alter table t change column k k tinytext;
show create table t;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

`alter table ...` should failed with `1170, "BLOB/TEXT column 'k' used in key specification without a key length"`

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

All statements succeeded. `show create table t` prints as following
```sql
CREATE TABLE `t` (
  `k` tinytext NOT NULL,
  `v` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`k`) /*T![clustered_index] NONCLUSTERED */
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin
```

Note that the `CREATE TABLE ...` statement will be rejected by both tidb and mysql. It may affect some backup/restore tools.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
master
